title: kernel-v1 privileged sensor event (v1)
description: One privileged-sensor event row as written by the kernel-v1 ring-buffer decoder. Carries the boot/cgroup/namespace identity required to attribute the event without naming PID alone, the validity bits keyed by field name so reviewers can prove which fields are trustworthy, and a typed payload. Sensor review forbids using PID, cgroup path, namespace string, or container name as a sole identity; this schema is the structured replacement.

boot_id.description: RFC4122 UUID identifying the kernel boot that owns this event. Two events with the same (boot_id, seq) are guaranteed to be the same record.

node_name.description: Node agent's hostname (or, in clusters, the k8s node name) where the ring consumer decoded this event.

agent_generation.description: Agent build generation string ('<crate_version>+<git_sha>') so reviewers can correlate an event row with the agent that emitted it.

event_id.description: Stable per-event identifier the consumer assigns after parsing; tied to (boot_id, sensor, seq).

schema_version.description: ABI schema_version of the row. Currently always 1; bumped on backward-incompatible shape changes.

bpf_link_id.description: bpftool link id (decimal digits) of the BPF program that produced this event, when available; '0' if the program was not pinned to a link.

event.description: Semantic event name (e.g. 'EXEC_RESULT', 'TASK_FORK', 'CONNECT_RESULT', 'DNS_PACKET'). The semantic names are the only ones reviewable; the schema forbids smuggling raw tracepoint strings through this field.

kfuncs_used.description: List of kfunc / kprobe helper names that contributed to this row. Reviewers use this list to verify a kfunc that is missing from a kernel cannot have produced a field that depends on it.

valids.description: Per-field validity bits keyed by field name. A field with valids[name]==false must not be used as identity or as a positive claim; the schema records it as unverified.

seq.description: Monotonic per-sensor sequence number assigned by the producer. Gaps indicate producer-side drops; reviewers MUST be able to detect gaps from this field.

ts_monotonic_ns.description: Monotonic timestamp in nanoseconds since boot. Combined with boot_id this is the durable ordering key.

ts_wall.description: RFC3339 wall-clock timestamp captured at the consumer; coarse enough to be a debug aid, never the sole ordering key.

pid_tgid.description: Composite (tgid << 32 | pid) reported by bpf_get_current_pid_tgid(). Combined with task_start_time_ns this disambiguates PID reuse across the same boot.

task_start_time_ns.description: Task start time in nanoseconds (clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)) reported by bpf_ktime_get_boot_ns helper. Same value as bpf_task_start_time; key to process correlation without PID.

cgroup_id.description: Cgroup v2 ID returned by bpf_get_current_cgroup_id(); 0 when the sensor did not query it or cgroup v2 is unavailable.

mount_ns_id.description: Mount namespace inode reported by bpf_get_current_pidns_inum(); 0 when the sensor did not query it.

pid_ns_id.description: PID namespace inode; 0 when not queried.

net_ns_id.description: Network namespace inode; 0 when not queried.

user_ns_id.description: User namespace inode; 0 when not queried.

uts_ns_id.description: UTS namespace inode; 0 when not queried.

ipc_ns_id.description: IPC namespace inode; 0 when not queried.

time_ns_id.description: Time namespace inode; 0 when not queried.

payload.description: Typed payload. 'kind' is a stable string the decoder agrees on; 'bytes_b64' is the base64-encoded payload (used for opaque payloads) and 'json' is the structured payload object. Exactly one of 'bytes_b64' or 'json' MUST be present per the producer contract; reviewers reject rows that carry both or neither.

bytes_b64.description: Opaque payload bytes, base64-encoded. Used when the payload is binary or when the producer chose not to render JSON.

json.description: Structured payload as a JSON object. Fields are payload-kind-specific; the consumer validates them against the kind's own schema.
